questions.stem: A sailboat has her sails up and her engine running and in gear. Under the Rule 3 definitions, what is she?
options: A sailing vessel, because her sails are hoisted
Not under command
Power-driven, as machinery propels her
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
questions.explanation: A sailing vessel is one under sail provided any propelling machinery is not being used. Once the engine is propelling her she is a power-driven vessel, even with the sails set.

questions.stem: Which of these is "underway" under Rule 3?
options: A vessel lying at anchor in a sheltered bay
A vessel made fast alongside a wharf
A vessel aground on a sandbar at low tide
One drifting, engine stopped, no anchor
questions.explanation: Underway only means the vessel is not at anchor, not made fast to the shore and not aground. A drifting vessel meets that test even though she is not under power.

questions.stem: Two small boats are on the fishing grounds. Boat A is towing a net behind her. Boat B is trolling with lines that do not restrict her ability to manoeuvre. Which statement matches the definition of a vessel engaged in fishing?
options: Both are vessels engaged in fishing, because both are fishing
Neither is, because fishing boats are only defined by their size
Only Boat B is, because trolling lines count as the main fishing apparatus
Only A: her net restricts her; non-restricting trolling is excluded
questions.explanation: The definition covers fishing with nets, lines, trawls or other apparatus that restrict manoeuvrability. A vessel using trolling lines or other gear that does not restrict her manoeuvrability is excluded, so Boat B is treated under whichever other category fits her.

questions.stem: Which description best fits a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre?
options: A vessel whose engine has broken down by exceptional circumstance
One whose work stops her manoeuvring as required, e.g. cable laying
Any vessel that is moving slowly in poor visibility
Any vessel that is anchored in or near a channel
questions.explanation: This category is based on the nature of the vessel's work, and a cable-laying vessel is one of the listed examples. An engine breakdown through exceptional circumstance is the not-under-command category. Slow speed and anchoring are not the test.

questions.stem: In dense fog you detect a vessel on radar about two miles away, but you cannot see her. Under Rule 3, which statement is correct?
options: You are in sight of her, because radar counts as observing her
Not in sight: that means seen visually from the other
You are in sight of her only if you also hear her whistle
You are in sight of her if she appears on AIS
questions.explanation: Rule 3 deems vessels in sight of one another only when one can be seen visually from the other. Radar, AIS or sound do not meet that test. This matters because it decides whether the Rules for vessels in sight or the restricted visibility Rule applies.

questions.stem: Which statement about a vessel constrained by her draught is correct?
options: It can be any vessel, including a sailing vessel, that dislikes shallow water
Power-driven, and her draught severely limits deviating from course
It is any vessel that has stopped because she touched bottom
It is a vessel whose work, such as dredging, limits her movement
questions.explanation: The definition applies only to a power-driven vessel, and the key is that the draught relative to the available water severely limits her ability to deviate. A vessel aground is a different situation, and work-related limits belong to restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.

questions.stem: A small cargo vessel loses her steering gear in open water and cannot keep out of the way of other vessels. Under Rule 3, which category fits her best?
options: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A vessel not under command
A vessel constrained by her draught
A vessel engaged in fishing
questions.explanation: A vessel not under command cannot manoeuvre as the Rules require because of some exceptional circumstance, and a steering failure is a classic example. Restricted in her ability to manoeuvre is about the nature of the vessel's work, constrained by her draught is about depth of water, and nothing here involves fishing gear.

questions.stem: Which of these is restricted visibility as Rule 3 defines it?
options: A clear, dark night with no moon at all
Heavy rain that limits how far you can see
Sun glare on the water at midday
A night when your radar is switched off
questions.explanation: Restricted visibility means visibility limited by fog, mist, falling snow, heavy rain, sandstorms or similar causes. Darkness alone, glare and the state of your own radar are not causes the definition names; they still matter for lookout and safe speed under Rules 5 and 6.
